title: Lumacaftor as a potential repurposed drug in targeting breast cancer stem cells: insights from in silico study.
authors: Pathak, Yamini; Camps, Ihosvany; Yadav, Manju; Mishra, Amaresh; Upadhyay, Jyoti; Tripathi, Vishwas
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过分子对接和MD模拟筛选靶向β-catenin的FDA药物，属于蛋白-小分子互作，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA体系无关。
abstract: CONTEXT: Breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) are a small subset of cells within breast tumors with characteristics similar to normal stem cells. Despite advancements in chemotherapy and targeted therapy for breast cancer, the prognosis for breast cancer patients has remained poor due to drug resistance, reoccurrence, and metastasis. Growing evidence suggests that deregulation of the self-renewal pathways, like the Wnt signaling pathway mediated by beta-catenin, plays a crucial role in the survival of breast cancer stem cells. Targeting the Wnt signaling pathway in breast cancer stem cells offers a promising avenue for developing effective therapeutic strategies targeting these cells, potentially leading to improved patient outcomes and reduced tumor recurrence. METHODS: For this purpose, we have screened a 1615 FDA-approved drug library against our target protein, beta-catenin, which is involved in the Wnt signaling pathway using molecular docking analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations. RESULTS: Molecular docking studies showed that the Lumacaftor- beta-catenin complex had the lowest docking score of - 8.7 kcal/mol towards beta-catenin protein than the reference inhibitor. Molecular dynamic simulations and MM/PBSA calculations were also performed for the Lumacaftor-beta-catenin complex to establish the stability of the interactions involved. Considering its promising attributes and encouraging results, Lumacaftor holds significant potential as a novel therapeutic option to target BCSCs. This study opens avenues for further investigation and may pave the way for developing therapeutic potential in breast cancer treatment. Further confirmation is warranted through in vitro and clinical studies to validate the findings of this study.
abstract_zh: 背景：乳腺癌干细胞（BCSCs）是乳腺肿瘤内一小部分具有类似正常干细胞特征的细胞亚群。尽管乳腺癌的化疗和靶向治疗取得了进展，但由于耐药性、复发和转移，乳腺癌患者的预后仍然不佳。越来越多的证据表明，自我更新通路（如由β-catenin介导的Wnt信号通路）的失调在乳腺癌干细胞的存活中起着关键作用。靶向乳腺癌干细胞中的Wnt信号通路，为开发针对这些细胞的有效治疗策略提供了有前景的途径，可能改善患者预后并减少肿瘤复发。方法：为此，我们利用分子对接分析、分子动力学（MD）模拟和分子力学泊松-玻尔兹曼表面积（MM/PBSA）计算，针对我们的靶蛋白β-catenin（参与Wnt信号通路）筛选了一个包含1615种FDA批准药物的文库。结果：分子对接研究表明，Lumacaftor-β-catenin复合物对β-catenin蛋白的对接得分最低，为-8.7 kcal/mol，低于参考抑制剂。还对Lumacaftor-β-catenin复合物进行了分子动力学模拟和MM/PBSA计算，以确定所涉及相互作用的稳定性。鉴于其有前景的特性和令人鼓舞的结果，Lumacaftor作为靶向BCSCs的新型治疗选择具有显著潜力。本研究为进一步探索开辟了途径，并可能为乳腺癌治疗潜力的开发铺平道路。仍需通过体外和临床研究进一步确认，以验证本研究的发现。
